methods.name: 16. If biaffine is competitive: boundary smoothing, no label smoothing, thresholded span decode
methods.citation: Zhu and Li 2022, Boundary Smoothing for Named Entity Recognition, ACL.
methods.why_it_applies: Baseline to smoothing: CoNLL03 93.48 to 93.65, OntoNotes 5 91.21 to 91.74, ACE 2005 86.56 to 87.15, Weibo 71.41 to 72.66, Resume 96.34 to 96.66. Label smoothing itself was below baseline on CoNLL (.1: 93.43) and ACE 2005 (.1: 86.31). RECIPE passes label_smoothing .1 into BiaffineSpanHead.loss, so rung C1's biaffine run is probably handicapped. BiaffineSpanHead.decode also uses argmax plus greedy overlap removal, which is weaker than method 2's rule.
methods.rule_reasoning: A loss and decode change only.
methods.expected_gain_slot_points: +0.2 to +1.2 on the biaffine variant only; matters only if biaffine reaches the Viterbi-decoded linear head
methods.evidence_quality: Medium: published on 8 NER benchmarks, some settings below baseline (D=2 on CoNLL). Authors saw no significant gain under synthetic boundary noise. Conditional on rung C1.
methods.implementation_sketch:
BiaffineSpanHead.loss: label_smoothing=0. Soft target tensor: the gold cell keeps 1-eps of type t; eps is split evenly over valid neighbours at Manhattan distance 1 (start+-1 or end+-1, start<=end, inside the mask) for type t; remainder goes to 'none'. Loss=-(soft*log_softmax).sum over valid cells. eps in {.1,.2,.3}, D=1.
decode: for each type take P(type) as p, keep p>tau, reuse best_set from method 2 and the table from method 3.

methods.name: 17. Knowledge distillation from an at-most-20M ensemble into one model
methods.citation: Allen-Zhu and Li 2023, Towards Understanding Ensemble, Knowledge Distillation and Self-Distillation, ICLR.
methods.why_it_applies: CIFAR-100 WRN-28-10: single 81.51, 10-model ensemble 84.69, distilled single 83.81, self-distilled 83.56, so most of the gain transferred. The rubric rewards efficiency, and a 4.34M student beats a 17.4M ensemble on that score. Measured ceiling here is small: 4-member ensemble intent 85.29 against best member 84.90, and full-stack slot 79.85 against best member 79.58.
methods.rule_reasoning: Teachers are trained on train only and soft targets are computed on train. Keep the teacher set at or under 20M total so the system-size claim holds at every stage; a larger teacher set would be gray.
methods.evidence_quality: Medium-low: vision evidence; the upper bound is measured here. The 4 members differ by hyperparameter rather than only by seed. Train-set teacher outputs are overconfident, so T matters.
methods.implementation_sketch:
Cache mean teacher log-probs on the train split, indexed by utterance id: intent 11,514x60 and tags 81,050x108 (9.4M values, about 19 MB as float16), with dropout and word dropout off.
Student loss=(1-w)*hard + w*T^2*KL(student/T||teacher/T) on intent and on tags[mask], T in {2,4}, w=.5.
Combine with mention replacement off, because teacher values are tied to the original tokens. Evaluate under full decoding.

methods.name: 18. Co-Interactive module after the encoder
methods.citation: Qin et al. 2021, A Co-Interactive Transformer for Joint Slot Filling and Intent Detection, ICASSP.
methods.why_it_applies: Replacing co-interactive attention with self-attention costs: SNIPS slot 95.9 to 95.1, intent 98.8 to 98.3; ATIS slot 95.9 to 95.4, intent 97.7 to 96.6. Against Stack-Propagation on SNIPS: slot 95.9 vs 94.2, intent 98.8 vs 98.0, ATIS slot tied at 95.9. This is stronger than the implemented bias, pooled-context and slot-to-intent links because each stream attends to the other per token, with label attention taken from the head weights.
methods.rule_reasoning: Architecture only, inside one model; label vectors are learned head weights.
methods.evidence_quality: Medium-low: small clean benchmarks, GloVe, BiLSTM encoder, CRF decoder. Overlaps with interaction, i2s and s2i rungs, and methods 1-3 remove part of the slot gain.
methods.implementation_sketch:
After the encoder: H_i=H+softmax(H@W_i.T,-1)@W_i, H_s=H+softmax(H@W_s.T,-1)@W_s, with W_i, W_s the intent and slot head weights.
Two nn.MultiheadAttention: query H_s over H_i, query H_i over H_s, residual and LayerNorm, each output through a zero-init Linear so the model starts at the baseline.
Then concatenate both streams, take the window t-1,t,t+1 per token, feed-forward, residual back to each stream. One block first (paper used 2).
Intent reads the pooled H_i stream; slot head reads the H_s stream.

methods.name: 19. Label names through Word2Vec: initialise label attention and tag scores
methods.citation: Wang et al. 2018, LEAM, ACL; Cui and Zhang 2019, Hierarchically-Refined Label Attention Network, EMNLP.
methods.why_it_applies: LEAM with name-initialised labels: Yahoo 77.42 vs SWEM 73.53 and fastText 72.30, DBPedia 99.02 vs 98.60. LAN with random label embeddings: OntoNotes NER 88.16 vs BiLSTM-CRF 86.99 and softmax 83.76. The implemented label attention uses a random intent query and has no slot-side counterpart. Micro-F1 limits the payoff: the 12 rarest slot types are only 0.98% of train spans.
methods.rule_reasoning: Label names are metadata and the vectors come from the same Word2Vec, with no new task data. Note that the current inventory is built from all splits, and I-transport_type has no train or dev example: train has 107 BIO labels, the checkpoint has 108, so it enters only through the test split. Build any label-derived table from train labels only, and consider building the inventory from train as well.
methods.evidence_quality: Low-medium: LEAM's table compares across published papers, and it gives no ablation of name-based against random initialisation.
methods.implementation_sketch:
v(label)=mean Word2Vec of its parts split on '_', zero vector if none found. Intent: self.la_query.data=proj(v(intent)); keep la_out at zero so reproduction holds.
Slots: self.tag_proj=nn.Linear(300,h), self.tag_scale=nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(1)); residual logits = tag_scale * h_tok @ tag_proj(V_type)[tag_type], with V_type frozen, 55x300 (count it).
LAN variant, about 40 lines: multi-head attention from tokens onto tag embeddings before the slot head, zero-init output.

methods.name: 20. Supervised contrastive term on the pooled utterance vector
methods.citation: Gunel et al. 2021, Supervised Contrastive Learning for Pre-trained Language Model Fine-tuning, ICLR.
methods.why_it_applies: With RoBERTa on full data: average 88.8 to 90.0, ranging from SST-2 96.0 to 96.3 up to QNLI 90.4 to 93.9. With 20 labelled examples: QNLI 65.0 to 75.7. Intent confusions are mostly between scenarios (77% of 307 errors), which is what class-level clustering could help, though the largest confusions involve the catch-all general_quirky.
methods.rule_reasoning: A loss on train batches only.
methods.evidence_quality: Low: pretrained-model evidence, not a scratch encoder on 11.5k utterances, and no numbers on joint models were found.
methods.implementation_sketch: z=normalize(nn.Linear(h,128)(pooled)); sim=z@z.T/tau, tau=.3; remove the diagonal; for each i with at least one same-intent item in the batch: L_i=-mean over positives of log(exp(sim_ip)/sum_{a!=i}exp(sim_ia)). total+=lam*L.mean(), lam in {.1,.3}. Projection is dropped at inference, but count its parameters.

methods.name: 21. Flagged track only: label-wise token replacement and shuffle within segments
methods.citation: Dai and Adel 2020, An Analysis of Simple Data Augmentation for NER, COLING.
methods.why_it_applies: Siblings of the implemented mention replacement. Full-data gains are small and mixed: LSTM MaSciP shuffle 76.4 to 77.1, Transformer MaSciP shuffle 79.8 to 80.3; several settings fall below baseline (i2b2 full: 81.1 to 80.6 and 87.8 to 87.7). Gains of +2 to +9 appear only on much smaller subsets.
methods.rule_reasoning: Generates new token sequences from train. The assignment bars adding examples and AI-generated task data, and the project already flags mention replacement for lecturer approval, so treat these the same way and report them on the flagged track.
methods.evidence_quality: Medium for the small effect size; domain datasets, not NLU.
methods.implementation_sketch: MassiveDataset._replaced: add modes. LwTR: each token with probability p replaced by a random train token of the same BIO label. SiS: shuffle tokens inside each maximal same-type segment, tags stay put. Add TrainConfig fields, and include them in the flagged expression in run_ladder.execute and experiment.run.

rejected.name: Hard intent-aware slot mask (planned)
rejected.reason: Measured on dev: 75.47 to 75.29 under the predicted intent, and even the gold-intent oracle only reaches 76.13. Hard masks kill true positives when intent is wrong (10 TP against 21 FP removed in the greedy count). Use method 6 if anything.

rejected.name: Joint top-k or slot-to-intent refinement from decoded slots (planned)
rejected.reason: Measured with decoded slot-type evidence added to intent scores: A1_ft_recipe 84.90 to at best 85.05, cross-fitted 84.80; A2_slot2 84.65 to at best 84.85, cross-fitted 84.65. No evidence of gain. Run last, if at all.

rejected.name: Large ensemble as the main lever (planned; de-prioritise, not dropped)
rejected.reason: After decoding the 4-member ensemble (17.4M) adds little: slot 79.85 against best member 79.58, intent 85.29 against 84.90. Its larger greedy gain was mostly repairing illegal tag sequences, which method 1 does for free. Spend cap space on the wide paths first (3-6M), then fill the remainder with members, and decide on dev. Members here differ by hyperparameter, so a seed-only ensemble may differ.

rejected.name: Late fusion of a separately trained SVM or tagger as the final system
rejected.reason: Gray to violating: a separately trained classifier supplying most of the intent decision looks like two systems. It is useful only as a fast dev probe. Put the same features inside the model instead (methods 4 and 7).

rejected.name: Meta-learner or stacker fitted on dev
rejected.reason: Violates train for training only. Only a handful of scalars (tau, gm, a, eta, gamma) are selection; thousands of fitted weights are training on dev.

rejected.name: Uncertainty weighting, GradNorm, PCGrad
rejected.reason: Kurin et al. 2022 find no optimiser clearly beating plain scalarisation on CelebA, Multi-MNIST or Cityscapes, with PCGrad about 35x slower on CelebA; Xin et al. 2022 find tuned scalarisation matches such methods. Here a plain scalar already moves a lot (lambda_slot 2: slot +2.35, intent -0.25). Extend the lambda_slot grid to {2,3,4} instead.

rejected.name: kNN or retrieval over train utterances
rejected.reason: Measured: only 11 of 2,033 dev utterances (0.5%) have an exact train match. A one-substitution train neighbour exists for 20.8%, where neighbour-majority intent scores 70.1% against the model's 87.0%. N-gram lookup (method 3) is the useful form of retrieval. Token-level memory would also strain the cap: 81,050 tokens x 256 dims is 20.7M.

rejected.name: Prototypical or metric heads
rejected.reason: Built for few-shot classes under a metric dominated by frequent ones: the 12 rarest slot types are 111 of 11,344 train spans (0.98%). No sign of gain for closed-set micro-F1, and label smoothing already softens the head.

rejected.name: Token shape features
rejected.reason: Measured in train tokens: 0.00% contain uppercase, 0.00% contain digits (numbers are spelled out), 1.17% contain an apostrophe. Almost nothing for shape to capture beyond the existing subword adapters; prefix, suffix and length are in method 7.

rejected.name: O-tag bias or threshold on tag probabilities
rejected.reason: Precision and recall are already balanced (73.00 / 71.77). Greedy with bias: 71.95 to 72.20 against 72.38. Viterbi with bias: 74.00 to 74.87 against 74.69, within noise. The span threshold in method 2 does this properly.

rejected.name: Per-type thresholds and intent-stratified mention table
rejected.reason: Measured and cross-fitted: per-type thresholds 78.43 vs 78.40 and 79.68 vs 79.52. Stratified table 78.60 vs 78.40 and 79.53 vs 79.52. Not worth the extra dev selection.

rejected.name: Mapping OOV words to the nearest trained Word2Vec row
rejected.reason: Measured without retraining: slot 72.60 at best, intent 84.60, and NonSlot-OOV F1 falls from 66.29 to 55.96. The raw Word2Vec vector did better with no retraining (slot 73.01, intent 85.24, Slot-OOV 49.67), so keep the existing flagged frozen rows.

rejected.name: Product or vector quantisation of the full Word2Vec table
rejected.reason: Measured coverage of dev slot-OOV tokens: top 46k extra rows 69.7%, 150k 79.5%, all 82.3%. Beyond the already implemented PCA-150k option the gain is 2.8 points of 254 tokens.

rejected.name: GCE, SCE, curriculum and co-teaching losses
rejected.reason: Published gains are under synthetic noise (GCE on CIFAR-10 at 0.2 noise: 89.83 vs 86.98). Noise and ambiguity here also sit in dev and test, so cleaner training cannot remove them: general_quirky alone has 59 of 105 dev errors, and with qa_factoid and qa_definition these are 32% of intent errors. Label smoothing already covers part of this (A2_ls0 78.75, recipe 78.60-78.64, A2_ls.2 78.98).

rejected.name: CrossWeigh or confident-learning reweighting
rejected.reason: Small gain for high cost: CoNLL03 +0.15 to +0.34, WNUT17 +1.07, using 30 models by default, and only about 25% of flagged sentences were real mistakes. Rule status gray: down-weighting approaches removal, and the assignment says no adding or removing examples. Hard removal or relabelling would violate it.

rejected.name: Focal, Dice and class-balanced losses
rejected.reason: They target imbalance, but the metric is micro-F1 and P and R are balanced; the O-weight variant already covers this direction.

rejected.name: AGIF and GL-GIN
rejected.reason: Built for multi-intent utterances; every MASSIVE utterance has exactly one intent, so the intent graph has nothing to model. The local slot window is covered more cheaply by methods 8 and 18.

rejected.name: SF-ID network
rejected.reason: Published below what the project already has in spirit: SNIPS slot 90.46 without CRF and 92.23 with, against Stack-Propagation 94.2. Its iteration idea is subsumed by interaction, slot-to-intent links and method 18.

rejected.name: Snapshot ensembles and SWA
rejected.reason: Their benefit is saving training time, which is not binding at 2 minutes per run. The measured ensemble gain after decoding is already small, and EMA covers the weight-averaging direction.

rejected.name: Deep mutual learning
rejected.reason: Same family as method 17 with a two-model training cost, and bounded by the same small measured ensemble gain.

rejected.name: Token-level or sequence-level mixup
rejected.reason: Utterances differ in length and BIO labels do not align, so interpolated tags have no exact-span meaning. Text-level forms would also create new sequences (gray). Intent-only mixup is method 14.

rejected.name: Pseudo-labelling, UDA or other semi-supervised learning
rejected.reason: Violates the rules on dev and test, as stated in the brief, and no other unlabeled task data is allowed. On train alone there is nothing unlabeled; adversarial noise and R-Drop already cover the smoothing effect.

rejected.name: Back-translation, BERT-based contextual augmentation, WordNet synonym replacement
rejected.reason: The first two rely on pretrained language models and violate the rules. WordNet is an external resource beyond Word2Vec, so at least gray.

rejected.name: Pretraining the encoder on external text, or on train alone
rejected.reason: External text amounts to a pretrained language model and violates the rules. On train alone there are only 81,050 tokens, and the implemented masked-word auxiliary loss already covers it.

analysis.label_noise:
Inputs verified first: recomputed Stage 1 gives intent 82.83, slot F1 66.09 (TP 1334, FP 691, FN 678); frame ids, gold tags and OOV groups all match the CSV.

Exact twins: 11 dev utterances (0.54%) have a casefold-identical train twin, each with one train row. Intent agrees 10/11 (miss: "what's up", dev general_quirky, train general_greet). BIO agrees 11/11 (7 carry a slot). Both agree 10/11.

Train-internal duplicates: 46 groups, all size 2 (92 rows). 4 conflict on intent (8.7%), 1 on annotation (2.2%), 5 on either. Pair disagreement on intent 8.7%, CI 2.2-17.4.

Templates: 10,521 unique in 11,514 train rows; 517 repeated (1,510 rows); 51 map to more than one intent (9.9% of repeated, 154 rows = 1.3% of train, 62 rows in a minority intent). Many conflicts come from the abstraction itself: "turn on the <device_type>" splits across wemo, hue, coffee and cleaning. Pair disagreement is 7.65% (CI 5.6-10.0), and 4.92% (CI 3.3-6.8) if the device value is kept.

Majority intent per template, where seen on dev: 93.02% on 258 utterances (12.69% of dev, CI 89.2-95.5). This uses gold slots to build the template. On the same rows: Stage 1 89.92, A1 91.86, linear 93.80. Keeping device_type: 96.34% on 246.

Because exact twins are so few, I added near-duplicate keys:
- No wake word or punctuation: 72 dev, majority 97.22%, pair disagreement 2.22%.
- Order-free content words: 292 dev, majority 97.26%, pair disagreement 4.74%, Stage 1 98.29% there.
- Nearest train neighbour with cosine above 0.8: 259 dev, label agrees about 97%.

Slot annotation on near-duplicates: 99.7% of 314 wake-word-key pairs identical; 93.3% of 2,264 content-key pairs identical, span F1 90.4 (CI 86.5-93.4).
analysis.ceiling_estimate:
Defensible upper range for dev intent accuracy: about 90-94%, central guess 91-92%. Evidence strength: weak to moderate, and indirect.

What supports it:
- Exact duplicates imply 91.3-95.6, from only 46 groups.
- Template majority on seen templates: 93.0 (CI 89.2-95.5).
- Templates keeping device_type imply 95.1-97.5, on short forms only.
- Stage 1, A1 and linear are all wrong on 187 utterances (9.2%), giving 90.8. This is a shared hard core, not a bound.
- I read a fixed random sample of 60 Stage-1 errors: 31 have a doubtful gold label or another equally defensible label, 2 are nonsense with the catch-all gold label, 27 are clear model errors. That puts about 9% of dev (CI about 7-11%) out of reach, so about 91 (CI about 89-93). This is one reader's judgement; labels are saved for re-checking.

Why it stays weak: exact twins cover 0.54% of dev. Template evidence covers 12.7%, is biased to short forms (5.69 vs 7.16 tokens) and uses gold slots. 87.3% of dev has an unseen template, where nothing measures noise directly and Stage 1 is at 81.80. Near-duplicates show only 2-5% disagreement but are the easy forms; cosine at or below 0.5 is 37% of dev, where linear reaches about 74. Reaching 94 overall would need about 91 in that region, which seems unlikely given general_quirky and qa_factoid.

Practical reach so far: linear 86.08-86.28, Stage 1 plus linear oracle union 89.97. Slot F1 has far more headroom: near-duplicate annotation agrees at 90-99 while the best run so far is 74.73. Re-annotating a sample, or checking published pretrained-model results (I did not look them up), would be stronger evidence.
analysis.intent_confusions:
349 errors (17.17% of dev). Unordered pairs with count and share of errors:
general_quirky/qa_factoid 23 (6.6%); news_query/qa_factoid 10 (2.9%); calendar_query/calendar_set 8 (2.3%); general_quirky/news_query 7 (2.0%); play_music/play_radio 7 (2.0%); music_likeness/music_query 7 (2.0%); qa_definition/qa_factoid 7 (2.0%); general_quirky/social_post 6 (1.7%); calendar_query/general_quirky 6 (1.7%); news_query/recommendation_events 6 (1.7%); cooking_recipe/general_quirky 5 (1.4%); general_quirky/music_query 4; general_quirky/weather_query 4; calendar_query/datetime_query 4; iot_hue_lightchange/iot_hue_lightup 4; alarm_query/alarm_set 4; takeaway_order/takeaway_query 4; email_querycontact/general_quirky 4; calendar_query/recommendation_events 4; transport_query/transport_ticket 4 (1.1% each).
The top 20 hold 36.7%. There are 167 distinct pairs, 93 of them singletons, so errors are diffuse. Four pairs tie at 7; examples cover the first two of those.

Examples (seeded random pick, gold then predicted):
- general_quirky/qa_factoid: "tell me something about america" (quirky, factoid); "explain to me about what different countries are represented in the book of revelation" (quirky, factoid); "wikipedia topics" (quirky, factoid).
- news_query/qa_factoid: "tell me about new york" (factoid, news); "how many runs did cheteshwar pujara scored yesterday" (news, factoid); "what is the seattle city council doing about homelessness" (news, factoid).
- calendar_query/calendar_set: "let me know the morning of my doctor appointment on the twelfth" (set, query); "notification of meeting on wednesday" (set, query); "schedule" (query, set).
- general_quirky/news_query: "what's been going on" (quirky, news); "tell me what happens when we die" (quirky, news); "who is leading the formula one race right now" (news, quirky).
- play_music/play_radio: "load spotify" (music, radio); "play nine hundred and seventy one" (radio, music); "i want to listen to soft rock" (music, radio).

Plausible label ambiguity: mostly yes for the top pairs, about half overall. By my reading, 38 of 55 errors in the top 5 pairs are doubtful (for example "when is my meeting" is gold calendar_set), and 31-33 of 60 random errors. The rest are real model errors, such as "switch on the lights" predicted iot_hue_lightup. A1 repeats 268 of the 349 errors, 183 with the same wrong label. general_quirky has recall 48.6 and precision 54.8; qa_factoid 66.7 and 58.3. 74.5% of errors cross scenarios; scenario accuracy is 87.21.

Per group (Stage 1 / A1 / linear; error share):
- No-Train-OOV: 86.10 / 87.84 / 88.80; 232 errors, 66.5%.
- NonSlot-Train-OOV: 55.70 / 60.40 / 57.05; 66 errors, 18.9%.
- Slot-Train-OOV: 76.28 / 79.07 / 85.12; 51 errors, 14.6%.
The NonSlot gap is partly mix: its intent mix alone predicts 76.96. Char-gram features barely help it, so it is not mainly a vocabulary problem. Linear's 85.12 suggests the Slot-OOV loss is repairable. Lifting both OOV groups to No-OOV accuracy adds at most 3.27 points, or 2.67 after standardising the intent mix.
analysis.slot_error_taxonomy:
Every FP and FN is assigned once and reconciles to 691 and 678. I added a sixth category, overlap with different type and boundary, because the five requested do not cover those spans.

Gold view, 2,012 spans: exact 1,334 (66.3%), right span wrong type 84 (4.2%), boundary same type 232 (11.5%), overlap other 73 (3.6%), missed 289 (14.4%).
Prediction view, 2,025 spans: exact 1,334 (65.9%), wrong type 84 (4.1%), boundary 282 (13.9%), overlap other 133 (6.6%), spurious 192 (9.5%).

Gold-view share per group (exact, wrong type, boundary, overlap, missed; slot F1):
- No-Train-OOV: 73.7, 3.8, 10.8, 3.0, 8.6; F1 71.51.
- NonSlot-Train-OOV: 65.8, 6.6, 10.5, 2.6, 14.5; F1 59.88.
- Slot-Train-OOV: 29.0, 5.6, 15.3, 6.9, 43.3; F1 34.51.
Spurious share of predictions: 8.7, 26.4, 8.7. The Slot-OOV group holds 16.0% of gold spans but 48.1% of missed spans. Spans containing an OOV token (225) hit 12.0% and are missed 56.4%; other spans in the same utterances hit 68.8%, so the damage is local.

F1 if a category vanished: boundary +12.47 (78.56), missed +8.95, overlap +4.67, wrong type +4.16, spurious +3.30. Slot-OOV group lifted to F1 71.51 or 77.78: overall +4.95 or +5.92 (joint +2.48 or +2.96). Boundary errors therefore outweigh OOV as a target, and 75% of them are in No-OOV utterances.

Boundary detail: 200 of 232 have the prediction inside the gold span ("new york city" predicted "new york"). Only 30 differ by function words or dots (F1 67.57 if repaired), so most are model errors, not annotation convention.

Illegal tags: 230 of 1,092 predicted I- tags are illegal (A1: 161 of 1,141). Dropping stray I- runs at decode time gives F1 68.14, +2.05 (A1 74.48, +2.10), with no parameters. Slot F1 is 68.46 when intent is right and 51.09 when wrong.

Top 15 types by support, F1 (support): date 82.4 (339), place_name 62.1 (209), event_name 65.4 (160), time 66.0 (137), person 58.8 (132), media_type 74.7 (98), weather_descriptor 79.7 (59), business_name 60.9 (58), transport_type 94.6 (54), food_type 58.8 (51), timeofday 83.0 (49), currency_name 61.5 (45), artist_name 50.0 (45), definition_word 74.2 (43), relation 74.7 (42).

Worst 10 with support at least 10: song_name 15.1 (23), radio_name 17.0 (21), general_frequency 19.4 (15), audiobook_name 25.0 (16), podcast_descriptor 26.1 (10), news_topic 36.6 (40), artist_name 50.0 (45), music_genre 54.5 (37), list_name 54.8 (37), food_type 58.8 (51).
analysis.linear_baseline:
Setup: TF-IDF word 1-2 grams (with the project tokeniser) plus char_wb 3-5 grams, 59,947 features, fit on train only. Multinomial logistic regression with saga, because L-BFGS history would break the memory limit.

Dev accuracy by C: 1 gives 84.26, 10 gives 85.93, 100 gives 86.08 (selected). C=100 stopped at max_iter and sits at the grid edge, so I ran a sensitivity check: C from 3 to 300 gives 85.59-86.28, and C=100 run to 1,000 iterations gives 86.28. The result is a plateau, not an artefact. Top-3 accuracy 95.08.

Against Stage 1: of 349 Stage-1 errors it gets 145 right; of 1,684 Stage-1 correct it gets 79 wrong. 204 are wrong in both, 107 with the same label. Oracle union 89.97, McNemar p below 0.0001.
Against A1 (84.90): fixes 97, breaks 73, union 89.67, p = 0.077, so not significantly better. All 11 finished deep ladder runs sit at 84.16-85.15 intent.

Per group: 88.80, 57.05, 85.12 (see intent_confusions). Word-only 84.60, char-only 85.24.

Size if used as a wide path: full 3.60M parameters; capped 20k+20k 2.40M gives 86.03; 10k+10k 1.20M gives 85.88; 5k+5k 0.60M gives 85.44.

Verdict on wide-and-deep: supported. It beats every deep run on intent at low cost and is complementary. Risks: it reaches 99.9% on train at C of 10 or more, so jointly it can starve the deep intent head and needs heavy regularisation or out-of-fold logits. It also competes with the frozen table for budget, and has no effect on slots.

Verdict on a separate linear ensemble: not supported as tested. A confidence-gated override with the threshold cross-validated on dev gives 85.54 with Stage 1 and 85.98 with A1, below linear alone at 86.08. It also risks the one-joint-model rule. A logit-level ensemble is unmeasured because Stage-1 probabilities were not available without torch.
analysis.coverage_curve:
Dev Train-OOV lexical tokens: 464 (3.32% of lexical tokens), 439 types; 254 in gold slots, 210 outside. The list mirrors ExtVocab: 256,856 non-train keys in file order.

Token coverage by K (overall / in slots / outside / Slot-OOV utterances with all slot OOV covered):
5k 37.3 / 28.3 / 48.1 / 25.6
10k 51.3 / 41.3 / 63.3 / 37.2
20k 62.5 / 53.9 / 72.9 / 49.8
30k 70.0 / 61.4 / 80.5 / 57.7
46k 76.5 / 69.7 / 84.8 / 67.4
100k 84.3 / 78.3 / 91.4 / 75.8
150k 85.3 / 79.5 / 92.4 / 77.2
all 87.3 / 82.3 / 93.3 / 80.0

Uncovered at 46k: 109 tokens (23.5%), 106 types, 77 in slots; 50 are in the list beyond rank 46k, 59 absent. By reading all of them (approximate at the boundaries):
- Ordinary words rare in or missing from Wikipedia: 36 (33.0%), e.g. bedtime, crispy, toggle, marinara, both.
- Names and brands: 34 (31.2%), e.g. cheteshwar, zaalima, beyonce, tinder.
- Possessive forms: 20 (18.3%), e.g. romero's, thursday's; 18 have a known base word.
- Typos and concatenations: 19 (17.4%), e.g. washingdon, metion, harrypotter.
- Numbers: 0, because the data has no digit at all.

A parameter-free lookup fallback to train words reaches 78 of the 464 OOV tokens (16.8%, 29 in slots): suffix stripping 64, possessive base 14. Edit distance 1 is too noisy to use ("poland" to "boland").

Largest legal K from a budget of 15,655,528 above the 4,344,472 base, with 4,731 train rows: ignoring the map, 47,454 at 300d and 151,824 at 100d. With the frozen_map the code actually builds (90,300 or 30,300 parameters): 47,153 at 300d (total 19,999,972) and 151,521 at 100d (total 19,999,972).
With adapters, 300d / 100d: BPE 46,657 / 150,033; char 47,031 / 151,156; n-gram 43,890 / 141,733; BPE+char 46,535 / 149,668; BPE+n-gram 43,394 / 140,245; all three 43,272 / 139,880.

Ladder sizes: ext46k alone is 19,654,072 and ext150k_pca100 alone is 19,847,872, both legal. If covered tokens behaved fully like train words, the OOV upper bound scaled by 67.4% coverage is about +3.3 to +4.0 slot F1 (about +1.7 to +2.0 joint). That is optimistic.
analysis.intent_slot_compatibility:
Train matrix: 432 of 3,300 intent-type cells seen (13.1%); median 8 types per intent, maximum 16; 126 cells seen once. Full map is in q6_intent_slot_matrix.csv.

Dev gold slots whose type was never seen with the gold intent: 16 of 2,012 (0.80%). A gold-intent mask would block exactly those, plus 70 of 691 Stage-1 FP spans (10.1%). With a minimum train count of 2 or 3 it blocks 1.74% or 2.39% of gold slots. Under the Stage-1 predicted intent, 72 gold slots (3.58%) would be blocked.

Stage-1 FP spans with a type never seen with the predicted intent: 33 of 691 (4.8%), against 9 of 1,334 TP spans (A1: 21 of 534, 3.9%). Most FPs are boundary errors of a compatible type, so the mask cannot see them.

Post-hoc span deletion, a lower bound since real masked decoding could also re-label:
- Predicted intent: +0.24 F1 on Stage 1, +0.06 on A1 (best threshold +0.38 and +0.06).
- Gold intent oracle: +0.97 and +0.89.
Re-labelling has a limited pool, since right-span-wrong-type is only 84 spans.

Reverse direction: a predicted slot incompatible with the predicted intent flags 41 utterances, intent wrong in 43.9% vs 16.6%, but that is only 5.2% of intent errors (A1 3.9%). Gold slots would flag 17.8% of errors and 0.4% of correct cases, so the signal needs better slots first.

Verdict: a hard train-derived mask is not worth effort. Keep it only as the cheap soft option already in the code.
analysis.other_findings:
Scope and limits: test rows were dropped on read and never used. Peak process memory 285 MB private, enforced by a 400 MB self-imposed commit limit, at below-normal priority. Beyond the listed inputs I read A1 and finished ladder frames, read-only. Audit labels are my own judgement.

Casing and characters: no uppercase, no digit and no non-ASCII character in train or dev. Numbers are spelled out, casefolding is a no-op, and a digit-focused method has nothing to act on.

Punctuation: "." is 208 of 212 non-lexical dev tokens, and 199 of the 212 sit inside gold slots, nearly all abbreviations. "am" is written "am" (train 303) but "pm" is always "p. m." (train 266, "pm" 0). 44 dev utterances end in ".". Spans with a dot have 29.2% boundary errors vs 10.7%.

Annotation consistency: the "five am" example is consistent (train 14 in slot, 0 plain, 1 inside a longer slot). So are today 524/21, tomorrow 220/2, this week 93/0. Mixed: meeting 279/26 (dev 48/8, and Stage 1 tags 7 of those 8 as spurious), "to do" 32/38, home 26/31. Boundary conventions truly split: date "next" inside 72, outside 51; timeofday "this" 22/18; business_name "at" 20/19. Type conflicts: weekend time 8, date 6; trump person 13, news_topic 8; us place_name 7, currency_name 6. 41.7% of spurious spans (80 of 192) have a (value, type) that is a gold slot in train; 67 of the 192 are in no-slot utterances (31.8% of dev has no slot).

Value history of dev gold spans, share and exact-hit rate: seen as this type 73.8%, 83.0; contains OOV 11.2%, 12.0; unseen string of known words 8.3%, 22.9 (44.6% boundary errors); plain text only 4.1%, 26.5; other type only 1.9%, 28.2.

Length: median 6, 99th percentile 17, maximum 27 on dev, so no truncation. Stage-1 intent by tokens: 1 token 64.0 (n=25), 2 tokens 69.6, 3-4 80.8, 5-8 85.1, 9-12 83.3, 13-20 78.8. Slot F1 drops to 57.9 at 13-20 tokens.

Rare intents: cooking_query has 4 train and 2 dev rows. audio_volume_other (18 train) has no dev row; music_album and transport_descriptor have no dev span. Intents under 100 train rows cover 155 dev rows at 84.52%, so they are not the weak spot. Macro recall 82.10.

Label inventory: train has 107 BIO labels and dev adds none, so the model's 108th comes from test only, because Assets reads all splits. I did not look at which label. It has no practical effect, but it does read test annotations.

Selection noise: joint SE is 0.70-0.73 on dev. Between close ladder runs the paired SE is 0.35-0.44, so differences below about 0.8 joint are ties even before seed noise, and greedy accepts any positive difference on one seed.

Possible unattended crash, from parameter arithmetic only, not from running it: in rung_B, B3 combines strict_best with the B2 winner. Any strict_best with the n-gram adapter (20.63M with ext46k), or BPE+char with ext150k_pca100 (20,033,136), trips the 20M assertion in build_model. run_ladder catches only ResourceAbort, so rung B would stop before its final confirm. Confirmed still present in the live run_ladder.py.
analysis.recommendations:
Favoured, in order of evidence:
1. Constrained decoding or CRF. Illegal tags are 14-21% of I- tags, and a zero-parameter repair already gives +2.05 to +2.10 slot F1, about +1 joint. Boundary is the largest error category (+12.47 F1 if fully repaired). Rung C's CRF competes against unconstrained argmax on the linear head, so about +1 joint of any CRF win may be the constraints alone; compare both with constraints.
2. Span-aware heads (biaffine, BIOES) for multi-token names: 200 of 232 boundary errors are truncated spans, and unseen strings of known words have 44.6% boundary errors. song_name, radio_name and audiobook_name are the worst types.
3. Slot-weighted loss. Slot has the larger headroom; A2_slot2 (79.69) is the best run so far.
4. A wide linear path inside the one joint model, zero-initialised and heavily regularised, at 0.6-1.2M parameters. Linear alone (86.08) beats all 11 deep runs on intent (84.16-85.15). Expect roughly +0.5 to +1 joint; this is unproven until trained.
5. BPE before a large frozen table: 0.15M parameters, reaches typos and possessives that Word2Vec rows cannot. Add the suffix and possessive lookup fallback (16.8% of OOV tokens, no parameters) as a strict-track variant.
6. Keep word dropout or UNK-robust pooling. Slot-OOV intent is 76-79 in deep runs vs 85.12 for linear.

Disfavoured:
- Hard intent-to-slot mask: +0.06 to +0.24 F1 with predicted intent. Rung E's soft mask and top-k are cheap to keep but expect little.
- A separately trained linear ensemble: no gain when gated, and it risks the one-model rule. Deep-only ensembles add little intent diversity (deep runs disagree on 6-8% of intents, A1 and linear on 12.5%); confirm whether any ensemble counts as one joint model.
- K beyond 46k with PCA: 41 more tokens at 100d for 15.5M parameters. If the flagged track is used, K of 10-20k gives better coverage per parameter, and it needs lecturer approval.
- Treating NonSlot-OOV intent as a vocabulary problem: char-gram linear reaches only 57.05.
- Hierarchical intent as a priority: 74.5% of errors cross scenarios, and those scenarios are fuzzy.
- Rare-intent rebalancing.

Target setting: treat about 90-94% as the intent ceiling and 87-89% as a realistic intent goal; expect most joint gain from slots.

Process: treat dev joint differences below about 0.8 as ties, and guard B3 against the 20M assertion before leaving rung B unattended.
